title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 10
text: “Well, we’ve taken care of that idiot. Let’s get back to the business talks.”
“Yeah, you’re right.”
“You’re so kind, Shield Hero.”
What’s so kind about that? I just blew your dad right out of here. Anyway, these guys are really light. That guy must be the cause of all this.
“Aaaah…”
Raphtalia is speechless. These guys are the ones who’re just letting it slide, aren’t they?
“Gwaaaaah! What the hell are you doing all of a sudden?!”
A figure bursts out of the chocolate swamp with a splash. Tsk! Did I miss my shot?

That’s exactly what I’d say. Tearing up someone’s letter of introduction out of the blue like that. One wrong move and that’s a crime. That’s how valuable a letter of introduction can be, depending on the person. I glare at the Robin Hood-like father while clicking my tongue.
“If you want my chocolate, prove your love for it.”
“Hmph!”

I stomp on a piece of chocolate lying nearby and kick it away. I hate guys who spout this kind of nonsensical nonsense the most. Part of the reason is that it reminds me of those heroes from before, but I just can’t stand people I can’t reason with. You could even say I loathe them. What’s this “love for chocolate” nonsense? There’s no such thing!
“You there! Get lost! I’m not giving you any chocolate!”
“That’s none of my business. I’m not buying from you. I’m buying from those two over there.”
“What did you say?!”
“To be honest, I don’t even want to know how twisted your so-called ‘love for chocolate’ really is.”
“You said it! Well then, let me show you the results of my research! You’ll be in agony once you experience my love!”
How did it come to this? I told you I didn’t want to know. Seriously, I honestly don’t want to know.

You can tell at a glance that he’s a researcher type, like Rat. But he’s not a level-headed person like Rat, is he? …Even though he’s become a bit of a caveman due to his fieldwork, he did understand what I said, right? It’s more troublesome when a conversation can’t hold together even though we should be able to understand each other. In that regard, Raph-chan is great. She picks up on my intentions even when we don’t speak the same language.
The Robin Hood-type old man staggers out of the swamp and slowly beckons me toward the field. I stride over to the field with an air of superiority.
“Watch this! My invention!”
Saying things like that, the Robin Hood-type old man digs up a potato-like vegetable buried in the field. His words and actions don’t match up.
“Here! Try it!”
I wasn’t exactly thrilled to be handed a vegetable, but when I saw what he’d tossed my way, I was taken aback. It was pitch-black… truffle chocolate.
“Well, what do you think? It’s one of my inventions: ‘Truffle Chocolate That Grows in the Field’!”
Is this some kind of cooking manga full of things to make fun of?! I shoved the truffle chocolate into my mouth and ate it. The quality wasn’t too bad, but of course, it tasted like dirt.
“Well? Your so-called love for chocolate is nothing in front of me! Everyone who fails to appreciate me is just foolish!”
“I was wondering what you were going to say—‘love’? No matter what it is, without supply and demand, it’s as good as nothing. Know this: self-indulgent inventions are the most meaningless of all!”
“What did you say?!”

O Robin Hood. I understand all too well why you ran away from home. If you had parents who thought you were some kind of genius capable of making a great invention—that’s just pathetic—you’d want to escape, too.
“Let me point out the flaw in this truffle chocolate! It’s that it’s hard to tell the difference between the dirt and the cocoa powder! Customers want chocolate—they don’t want to eat dirt!”

In fact, the truffle chocolate I ate had the dirt asserting itself very strongly amidst the cocoa powder flavor. But removing the dirt inevitably means removing the cocoa powder along with it. Washing it with water would only make the problem worse. I doubt anyone would want to eat truffle chocolate that’s been soaked in water. To begin with, water and chocolate are a terrible combination.
“And by the way, are you trying to say that ‘chocolate’ equals ‘truffle chocolate’? Besides, isn’t this just a subspecies of the chocolate tree? Love? That’s exactly what’s missing.”

The direction of his passion for breeding isn’t entirely wrong, but to call this “complete” at this stage is laughable. If this truffle chocolate had grown on a tree, it might have been passable. If it were a finished truffle chocolate from the start, there’d be no need for all this processing. If that were the case, I could say it had some potential.
“Let him say whatever he wants! Well then, let’s take a look at the next one!”
“Ah… It seems a contest of some sort has begun between Naofumi-sama and me.”

Raphtalia muttered in a fed-up tone. I don’t know about that. I’ve got to knock some sense into a cocky guy like this—otherwise, my business spirit won’t settle down. Let’s punish this guy who’s completely underestimated the business!
“Here’s the next one!”
The Robin Hood-type old man pointed to one of the fruits on the chocolate tree—a banana-like one—ripped it off, and tossed it at me.
“It’s just a banana! I mean, do bananas even exist in this world?”
That’s beside the point. Do bananas even exist…? Come to think of it, I think there was banana whipped cream on the crepe tree…?
“Hmph. That’s why you lack love! To think you can’t see my love. Go ahead and peel it!”
I peel the banana as instructed… and the inside turns out to be chocolate. I don’t get it.
“This is one of my finest inventions: the ‘Chocolate Banana That Grows on Trees’!”
Wait, doesn’t chocolate in this world already grow on trees? And anyway, banana peels are yellow—I wonder if, just like a real banana, the chocolate gets sweeter as it ripens.

…I take a bite. It’s just chocolate shaped like a banana. It’s not like the chocolate bananas you get at night markets. In fact, it’s not even banana-flavored chocolate. It’s just chocolate shaped like a banana. This is no different from chocolate wrapped in silver foil. Maybe the gimmick could sell it, but it’s a bit of a gimmick for kids.
“How foolish… This falls far short of what you’d call a chocolate banana. You’ve simply wrapped chocolate in a banana peel and made it ‘grow’ on a tree.”
“You… you wretch! To deny my love… Get out! Get out!”
“You kick people out the moment you realize they don’t understand you? You’re really taking the customer service business for granted.”

“My invention is something that those with an eye for it will understand! After I’m gone, future generations will come to love and nurture the inventions I’ve created! Yes, the times just haven’t caught up yet!”
“I was wondering what you were going to say… This isn’t a painting, you know? If you’re that passive, there’s no way you’ll sell anything!”

In my world, there are stories about famous painters—like the one known for sunflowers—who barely sold anything during their lifetimes. So, people who aren’t recognized tend to compare themselves to these famous painters and rant about how they’ll be appreciated by future generations!

But actually being recognized is the rare exception! There are people who work thousands of times harder than those who get recognized later, yet they fade into obscurity without ever being appreciated. Those cases are just a tiny, tiny fraction of the exceptions.

In reality, the fact that that painter’s works started fetching high prices was largely due to a shrewd merchant. He raised the value of a massive pile of Trash—which was originally practically worthless—and sold it. In that sense, while the painter who kept churning out work in large quantities was impressive, that merchant was even more so.

To begin with, if someone isn’t recognized for their work and ends up neglecting to even publish it, there’s no way anything decent could come out of some weird invention they come up with in a place like this. A hidden genius? An invention that gets recognized only after the developer’s death? Give me a break! Think about those of us who have to put up with the pathetic delusions of aspiring artists!
“I do think the invention itself is amazing, but… this…”
Raphtalia looks troubled as she samples this jerk of a dad’s invention. You don’t have to eat this piece of junk.
“That’s right. My husband is the type who’s always coming up with weird inventions…”
“Yeah. Dad says he’ll never sell his chocolate to anyone who doesn’t understand it, so our finances are in shambles… and to top it off, he keeps getting swindled by shady salesmen.”
“He’s being sweet-talked, isn’t he?”

The Robin Hood’s mother and sister nodded. That’s it. They’ll use some excuse like “sales cooperation” and end up selling it for a song. Since the quality is only halfway decent, they might actually melt down the contents and turn it into a different product. It just occurred to me… but that’s exactly the kind of trick the merchants I know would pull.
“You’re eating—besides the chocolate—the sweet lies that those who try to deceive you spout. Did it taste good?”
“But what you need to do is abandon your dreams—which are sweeter than real chocolate—and face the bitter… no, the dark chocolate reality head-on.”
“Grrr… I won’t forgive you! I won’t forgive you! Just you wait and see my great invention with your own eyes!”
“You’re still at it… but the caliber of your invention is nothing to write home about.”
The Robin Hood-like thief’s father turned bright red and ran off toward the workshop, where the smoke had cleared.
